routes.name: Dogna Crossing 25
routes.summary: Winter crossing from Val Dogna into Val Saisera. The course follows an almost 16 km valley road that may be snow-covered and groomed by snowmobile, then a forest track with repeated short climbs and descents to Rifugio Grego before descending to Kile Alpine Resort. Snow depth changes the character substantially from year to year.
terrain: snow-covered road or tarmac road depending on winter conditions
highlights: views towards Montasio, Mangart and Monte Lussari

routes.name: Valbruna 10
routes.summary: The course follows the Winter Wild Track from Valbruna through the length of Val Saisera to its highest point and finishes at Kile Alpine Resort. It is the most accessible winter route, with modest climbing and scenic singletrack through old forest.

routes.name: Alpe Adria Ultra 120

aidPoints.type: source/water point; exact supply type unclear

routes.summary: A 117.9 km alpine loop through the Julian Alps and across the Italy–Austria border. From Val Saisera the course passes Valbruna and Ugovizza, climbs to the Carnic ridge and crosses into Austria, follows the Karnischer Höhenweg via Egger Alm and Nassfeld, then returns through Val Aupa and the Prealpi Giulie before reaching Dogna and following the Jôf route back to Kile Alpine Resort. The route mixes runnable sections with long climbs, scree and technical alpine ground.

routes.name: Montasio 55
routes.summary: Point-to-point alpine route from Dogna to Kile Alpine Resort. The first 30.6 km follow the demanding Jôf Trail course to the only life base; the second half joins the Lussari route, climbs towards Monte Santo Lussari, descends steeply towards Valbruna and finishes with a gentler climb back to Kile. Technical uphill sections alternate with smoother, runnable descents.

routes.name: Jôf Trail 31
routes.summary: A demanding point-to-point alpine route from Dogna to Kile Alpine Resort. The opening six kilometres climb more than 1,900 metres and are described by the organizer as very technical and mountaineering in character. After the exposed high section, the course becomes faster and more runnable towards the finish.
terrain: faster runnable trail in the second half

routes.name: Lussari 24
routes.aidStatus: No named refreshment point found in accessible route-page text; official checkpoint table is linked and should be rechecked.
routes.summary: A new 2027 loop returning to Monte Santo Lussari. The ascent is largely on gravel, forest tracks and sections of tarmacked military road; the descent runs across ski slopes and through woods on soft but sometimes demanding ground. The route returns via Valbruna and a final gentle climb to Kile Alpine Resort.
highlights: descent through woods and ski slopes

unresolved: Trace de Trail pages for Dogna Crossing 25, Saisera Crossing 18, Alpe Adria Ultra 120 and Montasio 55 are marked Work in progress (temporary). Their measured values differ slightly from the organizer's Official Race Data 2027 page. The organizer says the official data page prevails; official table values are retained and Trace de Trail values are preserved only as temporary comparison values.
Jôf Trail 31 uses a rounded commercial name; the measured certified route is 30.51 km.

Direct Trace de Trail route pages and their explicit GPX notices were found for five routes only. For Valbruna 10, Grego 8, Lussari 24 and Oitzinger 12, the official pages link/embeds maps, profiles and checkpoint tables, but a separate direct route page with its own GPX notice was not independently verified in this run.
The organizer says GPX becomes available five days before each Alpe Adria race. No 2027 GPX binary was downloaded; metadata was not inspected.
Complete named aid-point details were not available in the accessible text for Grego 8, Lussari 24 or Oitzinger 12; their official checkpoint tables remain linked for later review.

Sardon Run 2027 is dated 21 August 2027, but the organiser has not yet published the final 2027 route list; 2026 routes (7, 17, 22, 48.4 and 71 km) are historical only. A 100 km non-stop format is in preparation, not confirmed as a final route.

Čaven Run 2027 preview announces a 60 km ultra and a new Čaven Vrh but no date or final route specifications. The event is jointly organised by Triatlon klub GPS and ASD SentieroUNO; separate rights-holder approval may be needed.
